title: Insadong 2026: Art, Tea, and Traditional Craft in Seoul
description: Insadong remains Seoul's most culturally rich neighborhood — art galleries, traditional tea houses, craft shops, and street food. Your 2026 guide.
content:
While newer neighborhoods chase trends, Insadong has spent decades being itself — and it remains Seoul's most distinctive cultural quarter. Korean traditional crafts, antiques, galleries, and some of the city's best tea houses cluster along a pedestrian main street and its many side alleys.

The Main Street (인사동길)

The main pedestrian strip is closed to traffic on weekends, becoming a festival atmosphere of street performers, food vendors, and pop-up art markets. On weekdays, it's quieter and more authentically about the shops.

Must-Visit Spots

Ssamziegil (쌈지길)

An open-air shopping complex built around a spiral ramp. Independent designers, craft shops, and small cafes. The architecture is worth seeing even if you don't shop.

Insadong Tea Houses

Several traditional Korean tea houses (다원, dawon) offer an experience increasingly rare in modern Seoul: sitting on ondol-heated floor cushions, drinking traditional teas in silence. Try Cha Masineun Tteul (차 마시는 뜰) — hidden in a courtyard off the main street.

Nakwon Arcade (낙원악기상가)

A four-story building dedicated entirely to musical instruments. Hundreds of shops selling everything from traditional Korean instruments to vintage electric guitars. Even if you're not buying, the atmosphere is unique.

💡 Shopping Tip: Prices in Insadong's craft shops are generally fair but negotiation is acceptable for items over ₩50,000. Many shops will package items for international travel.

What to Buy

  • Hanji (한지) handmade paper crafts
  • Traditional celadon ceramics
  • Hanji-covered notebooks and stationery
  • Traditional Korean clothing accessories
  • Antique furniture (check export regulations before buying)

Traditional Korean Craft Workshops

Try hanji papermaking, celadon pottery, and traditional Korean painting classes.
